title: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary: Understanding the Australian Average Salary
description: Learn how to calculate your annual salary from an hourly rate using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes tax, super, and the Australian average salary.
salarySummary: Based on a 38-hour week, your annual salary is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 hours per week and 52 weeks per year.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, this is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, $30 per hour gives $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. This assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the National Minimum Wage in Australia for 2026–27?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. Award rates may be higher.

faqs.q: Does the annual salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, on a $60,000 salary, your employer pays an extra $7,200 into your super fund.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

Understanding your annual salary from an hourly rate is straightforward. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual salary = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, this becomes:

**Annual salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It gives you a gross annual figure before tax and other deductions.

### Why 38 Hours and 52 Weeks?

The 38-hour week is the standard full-time hours under the Fair Work Act. Many awards and agreements use this as the base. Multiplying by 52 weeks gives a yearly total, though some roles may have paid leave that still counts towards this figure.

### The Fortnightly View

If you're paid fortnightly, your gross pay is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. Using the formula:

**Fortnightly pay = hourly rate × 38 × 2**

For example, at $30 per hour, your fortnightly gross is $30 × 38 × 2 = $2,280. This helps when budgeting between pay cycles.

## The Australian Average Salary

When people ask about the "australian average salary," they often refer to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings. As of May 2026, the ABS reports:

- Full-time adult ordinary time earnings: $2,083.70 per week
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): $1,579.20 per week

These are averages across all industries and states, not a median for any specific job. Your individual pay may differ based on your occupation, experience, and location.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour.

However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. Always check your specific award or agreement. You can find pay guides on our [pay guides](/blog) page.

### Casual Loading Explained

If you are a casual employee, your hourly rate typically includes a 25% loading instead of paid leave entitlements. When using our [the timesheet](/), you can check the box to add 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. Do not enter a rate that already includes the loading—the tool adds it for you.

## Tax and Superannuation

### Income Tax for 2026–27

The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) uses a progressive tax scale for residents. For 2026–27:

- $0 – $18,200: Nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% for each dollar over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% for each dollar over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% for each dollar over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: 45% for each dollar over $190,000

Plus, a Medicare levy of 2% generally applies. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

For an estimate of your take-home pay after tax and Medicare, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Superannuation Guarantee

Employers must pay superannuation on top of your salary. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $60,000 salary, your employer contributes an extra $7,200 to your super fund.

Super is not deducted from your pay—it is paid in addition. For more details, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents. It automatically applies the 38-hour week and 52-week year. You can also toggle casual loading to see the difference.

Remember: the annual figure is an estimate. It does not include unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, and tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold.

### Important Disclaimer

This guide provides general information only. Your actual pay and tax obligations depend on your individual circumstances. Always consult a qualified professional or refer to official sources such as the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Taxation Office, or the Australian Bureau of Statistics for precise figures.
